question: Should OpenClaw own a bundled, default-on Codex continuity and Telegram-control surface, or should this remain an opt-in external plugin built on the existing plugin seams?
rationale: This PR adds a durable operator workflow, startup behavior, configuration defaults, gateway routes, and a controlled write path; deciding its ownership and default exposure is a product and security-boundary choice rather than a mechanical repair.

options.title: Keep it external and opt-in
options.body: Retain the existing Codex commands in core and ask for a separately installable plugin that explicitly opts into continuity, notifications, and any write capability.

options.title: Sponsor a bounded bundled design
options.body: Accept bundled ownership only after naming the startup, configuration, upgrade, route, and Telegram authorization contracts and requiring focused implementation and proof.

options.title: Decline the surface
options.body: Do not add the continuity-control workflow if the bundled Codex plugin should remain limited to its existing agent-harness and command scope.

recommendation.title: Keep it external and opt-in
recommendation.body: Retain the existing Codex commands in core and ask for a separately installable plugin that explicitly opts into continuity, notifications, and any write capability.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision sits closest to the current OpenAI/Codex integration boundary, although direct ownership history should be confirmed before assignment.
